**Ten IRA owners missed part or all of their 2025 required minimum distribution (RMD), out of the roughly 30 who had one.** They fall into two groups.

**1. Five owners left their 401(k) RMD untaken.** HH-0120, HH-0236, HH-0371, HH-0664 and HH-5271 each signed one distribution form covering all of the owner's retirement accounts, including a former employer's 401(k). The whole amount was paid from one IRA. The IRS lets you add IRA RMDs together and take them from any one IRA, but a 401(k)'s RMD has to be paid from that 401(k). Each payment matches, to within a cent, the combined 31 Dec 2024 balance of the two IRAs and the 401(k) divided by 26.5, the IRS factor for age 73. So the IRAs are covered (overpaid, in fact). But nothing came out of any of the five 401(k)s, and the excess paid from the IRA doesn't count toward them. All five owners turned 73 in 2025, so the deadline was 1 April 2026, and it had passed by the 15 April record date. The CRM shows all five had retired, so the still-working exception doesn't apply.

**2. Five inherited IRAs had no 2025 distribution at all.** These are HH-0466, HH-0607, HH-7126, HH-0491 and HH-0842. In each, the previous custodian confirms the parent had already started RMDs before dying. The heir is an adult child well over 10 years younger than the parent. Under the final IRS rules, such an heir must take yearly RMDs during the 10-year payout period, starting in 2025. The custodian shows only dividends, fees and trades in these accounts.

**Points to check:**
- The life-expectancy and age factors aren't in the files. I used the standard IRS tables, so every RMD and shortfall figure is my own calculation.
- The inherited-IRA findings assume none of the heirs is disabled or chronically ill (which would change the rules). Nothing in the files says either way, so it's worth confirming.
- The records stop at 15 April 2026, so they won't show any catch-up distributions or late-RMD penalty relief requests since then.

**Checked and fine:** 18 other owners aged 73 or over took their full RMD, including those who paid part of it as a qualified charitable distribution (a payment straight to a charity). Owners whose 401(k) RMD was paid by the plan separately also met it. The four inherited IRAs whose original owners had not started RMDs owed nothing for 2025. The spouses who died in 2025 owned none of the IRAs.

I didn't do the fee, allocation and statement-reconciliation checks from the advisor checklist, because they don't bear on this question.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which IRA owners in the book had a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any of their retirement accounts, that was not met?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more owners did, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household with such an owner, each as {"household_id": ..., "owner_id": the owner's person ID, "account_ids": the accounts the unmet distribution had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
